business_scope.primary_industry_name: Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility Operations

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force 15 May 2012
Colombia-Canada Free Trade Agreement, in force 15 August 2011
Colombia-European Union Trade Agreement, in force 1 April 2013
Colombia-Republic of Korea Free Trade Agreement, in force 15 July 2016

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 2010 of 2019 and Decree 830 of 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB); Decree 1074 of 2015, Book 2, Part 1, Title 1, Chapter 4; Law 526 of 1999 (Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero - UIAF); Circular Externa 029 of 2014 of the Superintendencia de Sociedades (SAGRILAFT); Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. regime); Law 599 of 2000, Articles 323-327.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate power of attorney (poder) executed by each non-resident corporate shareholder in favour of the local legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or companies registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the foreign state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention, Consular Legalization through the Colombian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence, legal representation and good standing of each non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent public register of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport or national identity document of each foreign individual shareholder and of the appointed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of the document holder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives and beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, European Union restrictive measures list, UIAF Colombian control lists (including PEP-related lists) and the Superintendencia de Sociedades SAGRILAFT registry. The screening must be documented, refreshed at the time of registration and retained for at least ten years; any positive match requires immediate filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report (ROS) with the UIAF and suspension of the incorporation procedure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) at www.rues.org.co and the online services of the competent Cámara de Comercio (e.g., www.ccb.org.co for Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be expressed in Spanish; foreign expressions must be transliterated into Spanish phonetic script unless they constitute a permissible trademark or a personal name. The name must not be identical or phonetically homonymous with an existing registered firm and must end with 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' or the acronym 'S.A.S.'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended for one further 30-calendar-day period before expiry by filing a renewal request with the Chamber of Commerce and paying the registry tariff. If the requested name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal ('recurso de reposición') with the same Cámara de Comercio within ten (10) business days of notification, annexing the negative homologation certificate and the corrected proposed name. If the Chamber confirms the rejection, a second-instance appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be lodged with the Superintendencia de Sociedades within ten (10) business days. Judicial challenge before the administrative courts remains available under Law 1437 of 2011.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), arts. 1-21; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971) arts. 24-100; Decreto 1074 de 2015 arts. 8.1.1-8.4.3
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) - Registro Mercantil; Superintendencia de Sociedades (statutory supervision)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución y Estatutos (private incorporation instrument filed through the Registro Único Empresarial); public deed (escritura pública) required only when real property or registered in-kind assets are contributed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for S.A.S. (Law 1258/2008, art. 5); incorporation may declare subscribed and paid capital of any amount, expressed in Colombian pesos or foreign currency; payment of subscribed shares may be deferred under the bylaws; no escrow account is required; in-kind contributions must be described and appraised in the constitution document
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. 1. Share Subscription. The subscription of [NUMBER] shares by the sole shareholder, representing one hundred percent of the subscribed capital, is approved, and the capital payment schedule is ratified. 2. Registered Office. The registered office and principal place of business are fixed at [ADDRESS], Bogotá D.C., Republic of Colombia. 3. Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [NAME] as Legal Representative and [NAME] as Deputy Legal Representative, each empowered to sign documents, open bank accounts, and represent the Company before public and private entities. 4. Delegation. The Legal Representative is authorized to effect the Chamber of Commerce registration, tax enrollment before the DIAN, and to apply for the municipal operating, sanitary, and environmental approvals required for the multi-brand cloud kitchen operations. Executed at [PLACE], on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social) online platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter the RUES portal or attend the chamber counter; submit the homonymy application with one primary and two alternative corporate names; pay the search tariff (approximately COP 10,000); obtain the Certificado de Homonimia confirming that no identical or confusingly similar name is registered.
required_dossiers: Formulario de solicitud de homonimia
ID or passport of the incorporator(s)
Certificado de existencia of any existing corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If denied due to similarity, resubmit within 5 working days using the alternative names in precedence order; electronic resubmission on the same day triggers no additional tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the S.A.S. Private Constitution Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel and shareholders; notary public only if the capital includes real property or registered in-kind assets; Ministry of Foreign Affairs for apostille of foreign signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución in Spanish with full estatutos: corporate purpose (multi-brand ghost kitchen under CIIU 5610), authorized/subscribed/paid capital, share classes, board rules, legal representative powers, dispute resolution, and duration; execute signatures before an authorized witness. Foreign shareholders must deliver notarized and apostilled powers of attorney.
required_dossiers: Documento privado de constitución (original)
Certificado de homonimia (step 1)
Passport or cédula copies of shareholders
Apostilled power of attorney for foreign founders
Bank deposit receipt or in-kind appraisal report for paid capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry objections on drafting defects are cured by executing a complementary private document (documento aclaratorio) signed by all shareholders; notarial defects are corrected through a complementary escritura pública within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Chamber of Commerce Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) - Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed constitution document, homonymy certificate, completed Formulario del Registro Único Empresarial (RUE), pre-RUT data sheet, and proof of fee payment. The Chamber verifies compliance, assigns the provisional NIT, registers the company and its legal representative, and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
required_dossiers: Signed constitution instrument (original and two copies)
Certificate of homonymy
Formulario RUE (signed)
Registration fee receipt
Pre-RUT/NIT data sheet
Capital payment proof (bank receipt or sworn appraisal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file the corrective document with a written correction request within 10 working days; issuance may be expedited by requesting prompt review at the chamber customer service window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales - Sede Electrónica (dian.gov.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the provisional NIT assigned through RUES to access the DIAN electronic portal; complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) indicating the S.A.S. legal nature, fiscal address, principal economic activity CIIU 5610, tax responsibilities (Responsable de IVA if invoicing final consumers) and municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA); download the certified RUT.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal
Provisional NIT / Formulario RUE
Legal representative's ID or passport
Lease contract or title evidence of the registered office
Valid email and portal access credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the RUT for data mismatch, file an RUT update (actualización del RUT) within 10 working days; unresolved discrepancies are corrected via the DIAN service point with the registry certificate and representative ID.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Setup, Bank Account Opening, and Final Incorporation Closure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades; supervised credit institution; Cámara de Comercio (beneficial owner registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Stamp and certify the corporate ledger books (Libro de Accionistas and Libro de Actas) at the Chamber; register final beneficial owners under Law 2155 of 2021; convene the first shareholders/board meeting consistent with the constitutive resolution; open the corporate bank account using the NIT and the certificate of existence; archive the minute book and confirm that industrial and sanitary licensing applications may now proceed.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal
Definitive RUT/NIT
Constitutive board resolution
Beneficial owner declaration form
Bank account opening form and corporate background documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank challenges the beneficial owner declaration, update the RUT and Chamber records within 5 working days; if the Superintendencia flags governance defects, file a corrective corporate minute within 10 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: INVIMA - Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (food-safety certification) and the Municipal Mayor's Office (Alcaldía) through its hygiene inspector and Curaduría Urbana for zoning and operating permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Higiénico-Sanitario / Certificado de Condiciones Sanitarias y Licencia de Funcionamiento (actividad económica CIIU 5610 - preparación de alimentos para entrega a domicilio)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (SDA) - Bogotá, or the competent Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) in other municipalities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration - Exempted from full environmental license (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental not required under Decreto 1076 de 2015); subject to wastewater discharge registration (Permiso de Vertimientos) and an environmental checklist inspection.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer must comply with Resolución 631 de 2015 limits: pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 <= 80 mg/L, COD <= 200 mg/L, TSS <= 80 mg/L, and fats/oils/grease (FOG) <= 20 mg/L, with an approved grease interceptor; no significant VOC or particulate emissions are expected beyond domestic ventilation thresholds; solid waste must be separated per Resolución 2184 de 2019 and used cooking oil removed by an authorized waste operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety technical concept from the Cuerpo de Bomberos (Dirección Nacional de Bomberos) certifying compliance with NFPA/NRS 1000 requirements, including kitchen suppression systems; structural and land-use certificate from the Curaduría Urbana; occupational safety and health program (SG-SST) per Resolución 0312 de 2019 with ARL registry; and workplace hygiene inspection by the Secretaría de Salud.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). Official portal: www.dian.gov.co; transactional web service and registration via MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Colombian S.A.S. controlled by non-residents, the procedure is: (i) execute the S.A.S. incorporation document (written private instrument or public deed), appoint a legal representative residing in Colombia, and ensure foreign incorporation documents are apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish; (ii) register the company with the competent Cámara de Comercio to obtain the matrícula mercantil and certificate of existence and legal representation; (iii) apply for the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through DIAN using MUISCA within the statutory period, electing the tax classifications: national legal entity, income tax subject, VAT responsible (IVA), article-common responsible, and withholding agent where applicable; (iv) receive the definitive NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) after DIAN validates the RUT; (v) before commercial activity, enable electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) using DIAN-approved software, and if a non-resident primary beneficial owner exists, designate an attorney with sufficient power and Colombian tax domicile for service of process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a resident S.A.S. is a separate taxable entity taxed on worldwide income at national corporate income tax rates; its shareholders are not aggregate for income tax, and non-resident shareholders are taxed only on Colombian-source distributions and not on pass-through items. The S.A.S. has no partnership pass-through eligibility.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime for S.A.S. An eligible S.A.S. may irrevocably elect the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) under Articles 905 to 917 of the Tax Code provided it meets the statutory size thresholds, combining income tax, VAT, and other local taxes in a simplified filing. No separate hybrid entity election exists; anti-hybrid mismatch rules pursuant to Law 1819 of 2016 (BEPS Action 2) require the DIAN to recharacterize an entity or arrangement where the mismatch produces a deduction, and entities may elect their treatment only in the manner expressly authorized by the Tax Code.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto Sobre las Ventas (IVA) — Colombia's value-added tax system, supplemented by the national consumption tax where applicable to restaurant and delivery services; the system follows VAT principles with zero-rated exports and targeted exemptions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: COP 0 (no monetary threshold). A Colombian S.A.S. must register as an IVA responsible upon incorporation or commencement of taxable operations, even at zero revenue. Non-resident digital platforms supplying services into Colombia may elect to register under the simplified IVA digital-platform regime under Decree 2242 of 2017 and applicable DIAN resolutions without a monetary threshold; however, the local S.A.S. is a full responsible taxpayer irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing with DIAN fiscal clearance. Every sale, including ghost-kitchen deliveries to final consumers, must be issued by a DIAN-certified electronic invoicing solution and transmitted to DIAN through authorized web services (API/SOAP) in real time or at the moment of issuance; each e-invoice must contain the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) or CUDS code, a QR digital stamp, and must be transmitted in the XML/CBFE structure. Delivery platforms (Uber Eats, DoorDash) must be onboarded so that the S.A.S. is the invoicing merchant and the platform transmits order, payment, and settlement data to the fiscal software. Since 2021, all VAT-responsible taxpayers, including small service providers, must issue electronic invoices without reliance on printed-only documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Colombian VAT law, zero rating (exención con derecho a devolución del IVA) applies to tangible goods physically sold and transported outside Colombian customs territory to a non-resident buyer, and to services rendered in Colombia for the direct benefit and use of a non-resident entity or individual, where the service is paid with foreign currency and is deemed to be exploited wholly abroad. For ghost-kitchen and virtual-brand activities, local preparation and delivery to Colombian consumers is taxable at 19%; a zero rating is defensible only in cases such as export of packaged food products, foreign virtual-brand licensing, or a service contract to a non-resident restaurant group supported by the exporter's RUT export classification and evidence that the service is consumed in the recipient's foreign market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DEX electronic export declaration filed with DIAN and the VUCE foreign-trade platform
Bill of lading, air waybill, or multimodal transp ort document proving physical dispatch from Colombian customs territory

Foreign exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio) to an authorized Colombian bank, together with the bank's inward remittance certificate or liquidation of exchange, where the export proceeds meet the forex threshold
Proof of actual receipt of payment in convertible foreign currency from the non-resident buyer, with traceability to the corresponding export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN and the Financial Superintendence will cross-match customs export declarations, electronic logistics data, bank forex settlements, and destination-country evidence. If the zero rating is rejected, DIAN claws back the 19% VAT plus daily default interest and imposes the exactness penalty under Article 648 of the Tax Code (up to 200% of the omitted amount); issuing fraudulent export invoices for nonexistent exports triggers the corruption penalty, possible criminal tax evasion under Article 402, and forex-sanction liabilities of up to 200% of the unrepatriated or unsolicited amount. Refunds claimed for export VAT may be suspended and subject to criminal/administrative proceedings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Colombian Central Bank) jointly with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público) as the regulatory authority over the Colombian foreign exchange regime (Régimen Cambiario), implemented through the Comisión Intersectorial de Pagos and codified in Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83, and Decree 2247 of 2014.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia applies a managed floating exchange-rate system for the Colombian peso (COP), with unlimited quotation of the USD in the official exchange market (Mercado Cambiario) operated exclusively through authorized Exchange Market Intermediaries (Intermediarios del Mercado Cambiario, IMC). Current-account items, including dividend remittances, royalty payments, service-export proceeds, and cross-border marketplace payouts, enjoy full convertibility provided they are routed through an IMC and reported on the applicable exchange declaration form. Capital-account items, notably foreign direct investment in the SAS, are convertible only after compliance with the mandatory foreign-investment registration and exchange-declaration process; unregistered capital loses the right of standard profit and capital repatriation. Profit remittance to the non-resident shareholder is legally unrestricted once distributable reserves are evidenced by audited financial statements and the 10% dividend surtax plus applicable withholding are settled, but the remittance must pass through an IMC with the corresponding exchange form to obtain clean legal certainty. For the ghost-kitchen operator, marketplace remittances from US platforms qualify as service-export proceeds and are fully convertible, subject to the six-month surrender timeline and documentary evidence matching each settlement file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a Colombian SAS in the ghost-kitchen business, all export proceeds from services rendered to or via foreign marketplaces (UberEats, DoorDash, and similar aggregators), as well as any goods, must enter the Colombian exchange market through an IMC account within six months, counted from the dispatch date for goods and from the accrual or receipt term applicable to service invoices under Decree 2247 of 2014 and Circular DCIN-83 Title 11. There is no mandatory conversion percentage under the current regime: the SAS may retain foreign currency in a registered foreign-currency account (Cuenta en Moneda Extranjera, CME) with its IMC, but the proceeds must be credited in Colombia and surrendered to the exchange market declaration process in the corresponding form. Failure to channel and declare the proceeds within the statutory term exposes the SAS to sanctions, loss of access to the official exchange market for future remittances, and criminal-fiscal risk under the Colombian exchange-control regime. The Board must direct treasury to reconcile each aggregator payout report with the exchange declaration file, as under-reporting of marketplace settlements is the main audit trigger in the sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_file_requireme: Not legally binding as an exchange-control obligation; included as a governance step: each IMC channeling the marketplace payout must receive the export declaration (Forma 6 for services) together with the aggregator remittance statement, the corresponding invoice, and the proof of crediting, within the statutory deadline; the completed declaration is then filed with the Banco de la República's information system to close the six-month cycle.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is LOW as the primary treasury rail and MEDIUM only as a supplementary payout channel. Colombia does not grant foreign electronic-money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex a license to open local COP deposit accounts; any entity performing payment services in Colombia must be authorized by the Financial Superintendency of Colombia under Decree 2555 of 2010 and the SEDPE regime. Offshore EMIs may receive marketplace collections in USD abroad and make disbursements to foreign suppliers, but such funds are outside the Colombian exchange-market channel and therefore cannot be used for FDI declarations, statutory profit remittance, or payroll/tax payments in COP. The legally robust architecture is a tier-1 IMC account as the primary clearing and settlement node, complemented by local SEDPE wallets (Nequi, Daviplata, Movii) for last-mile merchant and courier payouts, and an offshore EMI only for supplier disbursement outside Colombia that are fully reconciled with the export reintegro flow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or high-assurance digital presence of the legal representative is mandatory in practice, while beneficial owners may be identified through certified documentation. The SFC's AML framework (Circular Básica Jurídica, Part I, Title IV) requires banks to complete client due diligence, corroborate the existence of the SAS, identify all ultimate beneficial owners, and validate the economic nexus of the business before opening a current or escrow account. Most tier-1 IMC banks, particularly Banco de Bogotá and BBVA, require the appointed legal representative to attend an in-person interview at a Colombian branch on the day of account opening; Bancolombia and Davivienda provide hybrid digital onboarding with biometric video-verification for the local representative, while fully remote opening for a newly incorporated SAS is generally unavailable. For foreign shareholders, the corporate documents (bylaws, shareholder register, board resolution) must be apostilled, notarially legalized, and officially translated into Spanish by a certified translator, and the power of attorney appointing the resident representative must be granted with the same formalities before opening the operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner controlling the SAS through a fully foreign-held shareholding, raising enhanced-due-diligence flags under geographic risk and risk-country screening by the SFC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Apostilled and translated Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (Certificado de Cámara de Comercio) issued within 90 days; (ii) notarized share register and the full UBO chain down to natural persons; (iii) passport copies and tax-residence certificates of each foreign shareholder; (iv) sworn source-of-funds declaration for the capital contribution; (v) an executed operational business plan, ghost-kitchen lease, and municipal operating license proving physical nexus in Colombia; and (vi) group organizational chart with a formal statement of the 100% non-resident ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Micro-transaction aggregate inflows from delivery marketplaces being flagged for split-transaction structuring or unrecorded informal FX conversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Executed marketplace partner agreements with UberEats and DoorDash showing payout terms; (ii) 12-month pro-forma revenue file with average ticket and volume analytics; (iii) an AML/CFT risk-management manual adopted under SFC Circular Básica Jurídica Part I Title IV; (iv) audit-trail mapping each marketplace settlement ID to its corresponding delivery order; and (v) a sworn declaration that all USD collections are channeled through the IMC within the six-month reintegro window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a foreign corporate shareholder domiciled in a jurisdiction not recognized as transparent by the bank's AML utility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Shareholder resolution approving the capital injection; (ii) the original SWIFT MT103 or payment proof evidencing the exact remittance; (iii) the Forma 3 international-investment exchange declaration stamped by the IMC at conversion; (iv) a legal opinion confirming the investment is registerable under Law 9 of 1991 and Decree 1735 of 1993; and (v) the Cámara de Comercio certificate reflecting the subscribed and paid capital and the updated shareholding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No verifiable physical corporate footprint at onboarding because the business model is delivery-only, prompting suspicion of a shell operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Commercial lease contract for the cloud-kitchen facility; (ii) municipal commercial license and food-handling permits issued by Invima or the local health authority; (iii) payroll and social-security administration records (EPS, ARL, AFP) confirming kitchen staff; (iv) geotagged photographic and video evidence of equipment and operations; and (v) a statutory declaration by the legal representative describing the operational status of the virtual-brand cooking sites.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital for the CO_SAS entity is executed through the following compliance chain: (i) the shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign corporate bank to the SAS's USD-denominated or COP account at the designated IMC bank, quoting the Colombian tax ID (NIT) and the foreign-investment purpose; (ii) at the moment of credit, the IMC files the exchange declaration for international investment (Forma 3) with Banco de la República, assigning the entry code for a fresh foreign capital contribution (inversión internacional directa); (iii) the SAS simultaneously registers the investment in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales using the bank's electronic system, attaching the share-issuance resolution, the certified Bylaws in Spanish, the Cámara de Comercio certificate, and, if applicable, proof of payment of registration-related taxes; (iv) the IMC delivers the certificate of existence of the foreign investment, which becomes the legal shield for future capital repatriation and dividend transfer. Currency conversion into COP may be executed at the IMC on the same value date or the funds may remain in the foreign-currency account for later conversion; conversion outside the IMC is prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements use a dual rail: (i) for foreign equipment and raw-material suppliers, direct supplier payments flow by SWIFT MT103 from the IMC account under the goods-import exchange declaration (Forma 1), typically code as advance payment or deferred payment per the underlying pro forma invoice; (ii) for larger capital purchases, a commercial letter of credit is opened through the IMC with an MT700 advice, commonly at sight with payment against ocean/airway bill documents, giving both legal and shipping protection. Domestic COP running costs (payroll, rent, tax, courier settlement) clear through the Colombian national payment systems, including ACH Colombia and the PSE low-value rail, while high-value interbank transfers use Banco de la República's electronic transfer system. Cross-border disbursements originating from the operational account must be matched with the corresponding exchange declaration; market- place payouts received from UberEats and DoorDash are treated as service-export proceeds and are surrendered into the IMC within the six-month reintegro window, after which the funds are freely usable for treasury operations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD deliverable currency forwards traded with an authorized IMC bank, limited to hedging an existing or committed commercial or financial exposure of the ghost-kitchen operation and subject to Banco de la República's documentary verification on underlying cash flow.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on COP settled in USD with offshore financial institutions, legally available to the Colombian SAS because the offshore counterparty falls outside the IMC perimeter, provided the settlement difference is declared in the corresponding exchange form when it affects a COP obligation.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between USD floating and COP fixed or floating entered with an IMC bank to neutralize the currency basis of a foreign-denominated equipment loan or a capitalized USD injection from the corporate shareholder.

Plain-vanilla European-style COP/USD options purchased by the SAS through an IMC bank, used to guarantee maximum COP costs on future marketplace payout conversions or import settlements without establishing a speculative short premium position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (annual commercial registry renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal after March 31 accrues a monthly or fractional surcharge of 1.5% on the applicable chamber renewal tariff; continued non-renewal for three consecutive years triggers administrative cancellation of the mercantile registration and loss of merchant status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial information update accompanying the RUES renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31, concurrently with the commercial registry renewal, using data as of the December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission prevents issuance of the chamber compliance certificate and may subject the S.A.S. to chamber administrative penalties and DIAN information-related sanctions under the Colombian Tax Code.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (annual corporate income tax return, Form 210)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the year following the taxable period, on the exact date fixed by the DIAN tax calendar for legal entities and based on the company's NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers the statutory late-filing penalty and default interest; continued non-filing enables DIAN deficiency assessment, administrative enforcement, and higher sanctions for omitted or inaccurate information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) annual UBO confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually according to the DIAN filing calendar, generally reporting beneficial ownership data as of the prior December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or submitting inaccurate beneficial-owner information exposes the S.A.S. to DIAN monetary penalties for unreliable or incomplete information, without prejudice to administrative inspection and enforcement measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) is mandatory under Colombian Commercial Code Article 203 when the S.A.S. has gross income above 3,000 monthly minimum wages (SMMLV) or total gross assets above 5,000 SMMLV in the preceding year; the obligation may also arise from bylaws or applicable law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian financial reporting follows Law 1314 of 2009 and CTCP guidance implementing IFRS: full IFRS for Grupo 1, IFRS for SMEs for Grupo 2, and NIIF for microbusinesses for Grupo 3, according to the company's size and classification.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must identify and annually confirm every ultimate beneficial owner, including individuals directly or indirectly holding at least the statutory threshold of shares or voting rights and any person exercising ultimate control, even if there is no ownership change; qualifying share transfers must be reflected in the annual DIAN RUB confirmation and in the corporate register of members.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 250 - US$ 1,000 per year depending on local office, registered agent, and corporate secretarial support selected
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 3,000 - US$ 8,000 per period for a limited-scope audit of a small S.A.S.; US$ 10,000 - US$ 25,000 per year when a full revisor fiscal appointment is mandatory
